sentences.text: Top module: m_spi_master.
spi_master is a single-clock SPI master with one slave select.
Each transfer shifts one byte out on o_mosi and one byte in from i_miso.
Software sends the bytes to transmit through a valid/ready command stream and gets back each received byte through a valid/ready response stream, in order.
The block never drops a received byte: when the response stream is back-pressured, the master stops starting new transfers.
One 8-bit transfer per command, MSB first, full duplex.
Bursts of any length: i_cmd_last = 1 marks the last byte of a burst. o_cs_n stays low for the whole burst.
SPI modes 0 to 3 are selected by i_cpol and i_cpha.
They are captured when a burst starts.
SCLK frequency is f(i_clk) / (2 x PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV), with PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV from 1 to 255 (fixed at elaboration).
Slave-select timing in half periods: lead time, trail time and minimum high time between bursts.
Back-to-back bytes inside a burst have no SCLK gap when the next command is ready in time.
Otherwise SCLK pauses at its idle level and o_cs_n stays low.
No received byte is lost under back-pressure: one byte is shown on the response stream and at most one more is held inside the master.
Asynchronous active-low reset.
More than one slave select, word lengths other than 8 bits, LSB-first order.
3-wire, dual, quad or DDR SPI, and SPI slave operation.
Changing the SCLK divider at run time, and programmable CS lead, trail or gap times.
Timeouts, error reporting outputs, interrupts, a register interface and DMA.
Synchronising i_miso or handling metastability on i_miso.
The slave drives i_miso from SCLK, which this block derives from i_clk.
Tri-stating or turning around o_mosi, and read-only or write-only transfer types.
Every transfer is full duplex.
Glitch checks at gate level and DFT/scan insertion.
These belong to the implementation flow, not to this verification.
ID: REF-001; Document: Motorola/Freescale SPI Block Guide (S12SPIV4); Revision: V04.01; Used for: Meaning of CPOL/CPHA and SPI modes 0 to 3 (leading/trailing edge, sample/shift)

ID: REF-002; Document: ARM IHI 0051, AMBA 4 AXI4-Stream Protocol Specification; Revision: Issue A; Used for: Valid/ready handshake meaning only: a transfer happens at an edge where valid and ready are both 1. The rule that TVALID stays 1 until the handshake does NOT apply to the command stream (REQ-CMD-004, GAP-004)
ID: REF-003; Document: docs/RTL_RULES.md (project coding rules); Revision: Current in repository; Used for: RTL coding rules
ID: REF-004; Document: spi_master design description (input of nnc spec-draft); Revision: 2026-11-19; Used for: Source of this specification
Term: D; Meaning: Value of PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV: the number of i_clk cycles in one SCLK half period.
Term: Edge; Meaning: A rising edge of i_clk. Edge E + n is the n-th rising edge after edge E.
Term: Cycle starting at edge E; Meaning: The i_clk period between edge E and edge E + 1. "After edge E" means in that cycle.
Term: Command handshake; Meaning: An edge at which i_rst_n = 1, i_cmd_valid = 1 and o_cmd_ready = 1. The command is accepted at that edge.
Term: Response handshake; Meaning: An edge at which i_rst_n = 1, o_rsp_valid = 1 and i_rsp_ready = 1. The shown response is taken at that edge.
Term: Transfer; Meaning: Shifting one byte out and one byte in for one accepted command. A transfer whose command is accepted at edge A covers the 16·D cycles starting at edges A to A + 16·D − 1.
Term: A; Meaning: The acceptance edge of the transfer being described.
Term: SCLK edge k; Meaning: For a transfer with acceptance edge A, the k-th transition of o_sclk (k = 1 to 16). It happens at edge A + k·D.

Term: Leading / trailing edge; Meaning: The odd SCLK edges (k = 1, 3, …, 15) are leading edges, which leave the idle level. The even SCLK edges (k = 2, 4, …, 16) are trailing edges, which return to the idle level.
Term: Sampling edge / shift edge; Meaning: The SCLK edges at which the receiver samples data / the transmitter changes data. They depend on CPHA (section 7.3).
Term: Last cycle of a transfer; Meaning: The cycle starting at edge A + 16·D − 1, which ends at SCLK edge 16.
Term: Burst; Meaning: The sequence of transfers from the command that drives o_cs_n low up to and including the command with i_cmd_last = 1.
Term: CPOL_b, CPHA_b; Meaning: The values of i_cpol and i_cpha captured at the first acceptance edge of the current burst.
Term: Idle; Meaning: Phase with o_cs_n = 1.
Term: Pause; Meaning: Phase inside a burst after a transfer with i_cmd_last = 0 ended, when no command was accepted at its SCLK edge 16. o_cs_n = 0 and o_sclk is at the idle level.
Term: Trail; Meaning: The D cycles after SCLK edge 16 of the last transfer of a burst, before o_cs_n goes high.
Term: Gap; Meaning: The time o_cs_n stays 1 between two bursts.
Term: Shown byte; Meaning: The byte on o_rsp_data while o_rsp_valid = 1.
Term: Held byte; Meaning: A received byte that is complete but not yet loaded into o_rsp_data, because the shown byte has not been taken.
Parameter: PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV; Default: 4; Legal values: 1 to 255; Description: Number of i_clk cycles in one SCLK half period (D). SCLK frequency = f(i_clk) / (2·D).
The block has no derived parameter visible at its interface.
[REQ-PAR-001] Elaboration of m_spi_master shall fail with an error message when PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV is less than 1 or greater than 255.
[REQ-PAR-002] Every value of PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV from 1 to 255 shall give the behaviour of this specification without any other change to the RTL.
m_spi_master: all ports (CLK)
Port: i_clk; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Clock; Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Clock, rising edge
Port: i_rst_n; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Reset (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Active-low reset
Port: i_cmd_valid; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Command stream valid. The environment keeps it 0 while i_rst_n = 0
Port: o_cmd_ready; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 1; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Command stream ready. Does not depend combinationally on any input
Port: i_cmd_data; Direction: input; Width: 8; Signal type: Data; Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Byte to send. Captured at the command handshake

Port: i_cmd_last; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: 1 = this byte ends the burst, and o_cs_n is released after it. Captured at the command handshake
Port: o_rsp_valid; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Response stream valid
Port: i_rsp_ready; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Response stream ready
Port: o_rsp_data; Direction: output; Width: 8; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Byte received during the transfer of the matching command

Port: o_sclk; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data (SPI serial clock; not used as a clock inside the block); Reset value: Equal to i_cpol (follows it combinationally); Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: SPI serial clock
Port: o_mosi; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: SPI master-out slave-in data
Port: i_miso; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: SPI master-in slave-out data. Sampled by i_clk without a synchroniser
Port: o_cs_n; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 1; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: SPI slave select, active low

Port: i_cpol; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Data (quasi-static configuration); Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: SPI clock polarity (SCLK idle level). May change only while o_cs_n = 1

Port: i_cpha; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Data (quasi-static configuration); Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: SPI clock phase. 0 = sample on leading edges, 1 = sample on trailing edges. May change only while o_cs_n = 1
[REQ-CLK-001] All state elements of m_spi_master shall be clocked by the rising edge of i_clk, which is the only clock of the block (domain CLK).
[REQ-CLK-002] o_sclk shall be produced as a data output timed by i_clk and shall not clock any state element inside the block.
[REQ-CLK-003] i_miso shall be treated as synchronous to i_clk and shall be sampled without a synchroniser, because the slave launches it from o_sclk, which is derived from i_clk.
All inputs are synchronous to i_clk.
The block has no clock-domain crossing.
[REQ-RST-001] When i_rst_n changes to 0, all outputs shall take their reset values at once, without waiting for an edge of i_clk.
[REQ-RST-002] While i_rst_n = 0, o_cs_n shall be 1.
[REQ-RST-003] While i_rst_n = 0, o_sclk shall be equal to the current value of i_cpol and shall follow every change of i_cpol combinationally.
[REQ-RST-004] While i_rst_n = 0, o_mosi shall be 0.
[REQ-RST-005] While i_rst_n = 0, o_rsp_valid shall be 0 and o_rsp_data shall be 8'h00.
[REQ-RST-006] While i_rst_n = 0, o_cmd_ready shall be 1.
[REQ-RST-007] While i_rst_n = 0, the master shall not accept a command, whatever the values of i_cmd_valid and o_cmd_ready.
[REQ-RST-008] Reset asserted during a burst shall abort the transfer in progress, and no response shall be produced for that transfer.
[REQ-RST-009] Reset asserted while a shown byte or a held byte exists shall discard that byte without a response handshake.
[REQ-RST-010] After i_rst_n returns to 1, the master shall be in Idle with the gap requirement met: it can accept a command at the first edge at which i_rst_n is 1.

[REQ-RST-011] The minimum o_cs_n high time of REQ-CS-005 shall not be required across a reset: the high time of o_cs_n after an aborted burst is the reset duration plus the time until the next acceptance.
i_rst_n is released synchronously to i_clk by the environment (ENV-001).
This section uses the terms of section 3.
D = PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV.
The phases of the block are:
Phase: Reset (i_rst_n = 0); o_cs_n: 1; o_sclk: i_cpol (combinational); o_mosi: 0; o_cmd_ready: 1
Phase: Idle; o_cs_n: 1; o_sclk: i_cpol (combinational); o_mosi: Holds last value; o_cmd_ready: 0 in the first D − 1 cycles after o_cs_n rose, otherwise NOT o_rsp_valid
Phase: Transfer; o_cs_n: 0; o_sclk: Toggles at edges A + k·D, k = 1 to 16; o_mosi: Section 7.5; o_cmd_ready: 0, except in the last cycle: 1 if i_cmd_last of this transfer = 0 and o_rsp_valid = 0
Phase: Pause; o_cs_n: 0; o_sclk: CPOL_b; o_mosi: Holds last value; o_cmd_ready: NOT o_rsp_valid
Phase: Trail; o_cs_n: 0; o_sclk: CPOL_b; o_mosi: Holds last value; o_cmd_ready: 0
Phase changes (all at edges, except reset):
From: Idle; Condition: Command handshake at edge A; To: Transfer (first of a burst)
From: Transfer; Condition: Edge A + 16·D, command handshake at this edge; To: Transfer (next byte, no gap)
From: Transfer; Condition: Edge A + 16·D, no handshake, i_cmd_last of this transfer = 0; To: Pause
From: Transfer; Condition: Edge A + 16·D, i_cmd_last of this transfer = 1; To: Trail
From: Pause; Condition: Command handshake; To: Transfer
From: Trail; Condition: Edge A + 17·D; To: Idle
From: Any; Condition: i_rst_n = 0; To: Reset
[REQ-CMD-001] The master shall accept a command at an edge only when i_rst_n = 1, i_cmd_valid = 1 and o_cmd_ready = 1 at that edge.
[REQ-CMD-002] At the acceptance edge the master shall capture i_cmd_data as the byte to send and i_cmd_last as the end-of-burst flag of that transfer.
[REQ-CMD-003] The values of i_cmd_data and i_cmd_last at edges without a command handshake shall have no effect.
[REQ-CMD-004] If i_cmd_valid goes from 1 to 0 without a command handshake, the master shall behave as if the command had never been presented.
[REQ-CMD-005] o_cmd_ready shall change only at an edge of i_clk or when i_rst_n is asserted, and shall not depend combinationally on any input.
[REQ-CMD-006] While i_rst_n = 1, o_cmd_ready shall be 0 in every cycle in which o_rsp_valid = 1.
[REQ-CMD-007] When o_cs_n changes from 0 to 1 at edge R, o_cmd_ready shall be 0 in every cycle that starts at an edge from R to R + D − 2.
When D = 1 there is no such cycle.
[REQ-CMD-008] In Idle, o_cmd_ready shall be 1 when o_rsp_valid = 0 in every cycle that starts at edge R + D − 1 or later, and in every cycle after reset release until the next acceptance.
[REQ-CMD-009] During a transfer, o_cmd_ready shall be 0 in every cycle except the last cycle of the transfer.
[REQ-CMD-010] In the last cycle of a transfer, o_cmd_ready shall be 1 if the i_cmd_last captured for that transfer is 0 and o_rsp_valid is 0, and 0 otherwise.
[REQ-CMD-011] In Pause, o_cmd_ready shall be 1 when o_rsp_valid = 0 and 0 when o_rsp_valid = 1.
[REQ-CMD-012] In Trail, o_cmd_ready shall be 0.
[REQ-CS-001] A command accepted in Idle at edge A shall start a burst: o_cs_n shall change from 1 to 0 at edge A.
[REQ-CS-002] o_cs_n shall stay 0 from the start of a burst until edge A + 17·D, where A is the acceptance edge of the transfer whose captured i_cmd_last is 1.
At that edge o_cs_n shall change to 1.
[REQ-CS-003] o_cs_n shall change only at the edges given in REQ-CS-001 and REQ-CS-002, and at the assertion of i_rst_n.
[REQ-CS-004] The first SCLK edge of a burst shall come exactly D cycles after o_cs_n falls (edge A + D), so the lead time is one SCLK half period.
[REQ-CS-005] Between two bursts with no reset in between, o_cs_n shall stay 1 for at least D cycles.
[REQ-CS-006] o_cs_n shall rise exactly D cycles after SCLK edge 16 of the last transfer of the burst, so the trail time is one SCLK half period.
[REQ-CS-007] The rise of o_cs_n at the end of a burst shall not depend on the state of the response stream (o_rsp_valid, i_rsp_ready, a held byte).
REQ-CS-005 follows from REQ-CMD-007: the earliest acceptance after o_cs_n rises at edge R is edge R + D.
[REQ-MODE-001] At the acceptance edge of the first command of a burst, the master shall capture i_cpol as CPOL_b and i_cpha as CPHA_b.
[REQ-MODE-002] CPOL_b and CPHA_b shall control o_sclk, o_mosi and the sampling of i_miso for the whole burst, including Pause and Trail.
[REQ-MODE-003] Changes of i_cpol or i_cpha while o_cs_n = 0 shall have no effect on o_sclk, o_mosi, o_cs_n, the sampling of i_miso or the response data.
[REQ-MODE-004] With CPHA_b = 0, the leading SCLK edges (odd k) shall be the sampling edges and the trailing SCLK edges (even k) shall be the shift edges.
[REQ-MODE-005] With CPHA_b = 1, the leading SCLK edges (odd k) shall be the shift edges and the trailing SCLK edges (even k) shall be the sampling edges.

Mode: 0; i_cpol: 0; i_cpha: 0; Idle o_sclk: 0; Leading edges (k odd): Rising, sample; Trailing edges (k even): Falling, shift; o_mosi bit 7 launched at: Acceptance edge A; i_miso sampled at: Edges A + (2j+1)·D

Mode: 1; i_cpol: 0; i_cpha: 1; Idle o_sclk: 0; Leading edges (k odd): Rising, shift; Trailing edges (k even): Falling, sample; o_mosi bit 7 launched at: SCLK edge 1 (A + D); i_miso sampled at: Edges A + (2j+2)·D

Mode: 2; i_cpol: 1; i_cpha: 0; Idle o_sclk: 1; Leading edges (k odd): Falling, sample; Trailing edges (k even): Rising, shift; o_mosi bit 7 launched at: Acceptance edge A; i_miso sampled at: Edges A + (2j+1)·D

Mode: 3; i_cpol: 1; i_cpha: 1; Idle o_sclk: 1; Leading edges (k odd): Falling, shift; Trailing edges (k even): Rising, sample; o_mosi bit 7 launched at: SCLK edge 1 (A + D); i_miso sampled at: Edges A + (2j+2)·D
Bit 7 − j is transmitted and received in step j.)
[REQ-SCLK-001] For a transfer with acceptance edge A, o_sclk shall toggle at each of the 16 edges A + k·D, k = 1 to 16.
[REQ-SCLK-002] While o_cs_n = 0, o_sclk shall not change at any edge other than those of REQ-SCLK-001.
[REQ-SCLK-003] While o_cs_n = 0 and no transfer is between its SCLK edges 1 and 16, o_sclk shall equal CPOL_b.
This covers the lead half period, Pause and Trail.
[REQ-SCLK-004] After SCLK edge k of a transfer, o_sclk shall equal NOT CPOL_b for odd k and CPOL_b for even k.
[REQ-SCLK-005] While o_cs_n = 1, o_sclk shall equal i_cpol and shall follow changes of i_cpol combinationally.
[REQ-SCLK-006] When o_cs_n rises at edge R, o_sclk shall take the value of i_cpol from edge R on.
[REQ-SCLK-007] When a transfer starts at SCLK edge 16 of the previous transfer of the same burst, the SCLK period over the joint shall be 2·D cycles with each half period equal to D cycles.
The byte to send is d[7:0] = the captured i_cmd_data.
[REQ-MOSI-001] The bits of each byte shall be sent in the order d[7], d[6], …, d[0] (MSB first).
[REQ-MOSI-002] With CPHA_b = 0, o_mosi shall take the value d[7] at the acceptance edge A.
[REQ-MOSI-003] With CPHA_b = 0, o_mosi shall take the value d[7 − j] at edge A + 2·j·D for j = 1 to 7 (SCLK edges 2, 4, …, 14).
[REQ-MOSI-004] With CPHA_b = 1, o_mosi shall take the value d[7 − j] at edge A + (2·j + 1)·D for j = 0 to 7 (SCLK edges 1, 3, …, 15).
[REQ-MOSI-005] o_mosi shall not change at any edge other than those of REQ-MOSI-002 to REQ-MOSI-004, except at the assertion of i_rst_n.
[REQ-MOSI-006] In Idle, Pause and Trail, o_mosi shall keep the last value it was given.
That value is 0 after reset.
[REQ-MOSI-007] o_mosi shall be stable in the cycle before each sampling edge and shall not change at any sampling edge, in all four modes.
With CPHA_b = 0, o_mosi keeps d[0] after SCLK edge 16 unless the next command is accepted at that edge, in which case it takes the next d[7] at that edge (REQ-MOSI-002).
With CPHA_b = 1, o_mosi keeps its previous value from the acceptance edge until SCLK edge 1.
[REQ-MISO-001] With CPHA_b = 0, the master shall capture i_miso as received bit r[7 − j] at edge A + (2·j + 1)·D for j = 0 to 7.
[REQ-MISO-002] With CPHA_b = 1, the master shall capture i_miso as received bit r[7 − j] at edge A + (2·j + 2)·D for j = 0 to 7.
[REQ-MISO-003] The value captured at a sampling edge shall be the value of i_miso in the cycle that ends at that edge, which is the value just before o_sclk makes the sampling transition.
[REQ-MISO-004] i_miso shall have no effect at any edge other than the sampling edges of a transfer.
[REQ-MISO-005] The received byte r[7:0] of a transfer shall be made of the 8 bits captured during that transfer only.
[REQ-RSP-001] Each accepted command shall produce exactly one response carrying the byte received during its transfer.
[REQ-RSP-002] Responses shall be delivered in the order in which the commands were accepted, across burst boundaries.

[REQ-RSP-003] At edge A + 16·D of a transfer, the master shall load the received byte into o_rsp_data and set o_rsp_valid to 1 if o_rsp_valid was 0 in the cycle ending at that edge or a response handshake occurs at that edge.
[REQ-RSP-004] If neither condition of REQ-RSP-003 holds at edge A + 16·D, the received byte shall become the held byte.
[REQ-RSP-005] At the edge where the response handshake of the shown byte occurs, the held byte shall be loaded into o_rsp_data and o_rsp_valid shall stay 1.
[REQ-RSP-006] At a response handshake where no byte is loaded at the same edge, o_rsp_valid shall change to 0.
[REQ-RSP-007] While o_rsp_valid = 1 and no response handshake has occurred, o_rsp_valid shall stay 1 and o_rsp_data shall not change.
[REQ-RSP-008] While o_rsp_valid = 0, o_rsp_data shall keep the last byte loaded into it, or 8'h00 after reset.
[REQ-RSP-009] o_rsp_valid and o_rsp_data shall change only at edges of i_clk or at the assertion of i_rst_n.
[REQ-RSP-010] i_rsp_ready shall have no effect while o_rsp_valid = 0.
[REQ-RSP-011] The master shall never overwrite a shown byte or a held byte before it has been taken, and shall never deliver a byte twice.
[REQ-RSP-012] At any time, at most two received bytes shall be pending: one shown byte and at most one held byte.
The pending-byte limit holds because REQ-CMD-006 blocks the start of a transfer while o_rsp_valid = 1.
A new transfer therefore starts only when every earlier received byte has been taken, except the byte of the transfer that ends at the same edge.

sections.title: Continuation, pause and end of burst

sentences.text: [REQ-FLOW-001] When a command is accepted at edge A + 16·D of a transfer whose captured i_cmd_last is 0, the new transfer shall use that edge as its acceptance edge.
Its SCLK edge 1 then comes D cycles after SCLK edge 16 of the previous transfer, with no gap.
[REQ-FLOW-002] When a transfer with captured i_cmd_last = 0 ends at edge A + 16·D without a command handshake at that edge, the master shall enter Pause.
[REQ-FLOW-003] In Pause, o_cs_n shall stay 0, o_sclk shall stay at CPOL_b and o_mosi shall keep its value.
[REQ-FLOW-004] Pause shall last until a command is accepted, without any time limit.
[REQ-FLOW-005] A command accepted in Pause at edge P shall start a transfer with acceptance edge A = P, in the same burst and with the same CPOL_b and CPHA_b.
[REQ-FLOW-006] When a transfer with captured i_cmd_last = 1 ends at edge A + 16·D, the master shall enter Trail, and o_cs_n shall rise at edge A + 17·D (REQ-CS-002).
[REQ-FLOW-007] The master shall not start a transfer while a received byte is held.
Latency and throughput (D = PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV, all numbers in i_clk cycles):
Item: Command acceptance to o_cs_n low (first byte of a burst); Value: 0 (same edge A)
Item: Command acceptance to SCLK edge 1 (lead); Value: D
Item: Command acceptance to o_rsp_valid = 1 (response register free); Value: 16·D
Item: SCLK edge 16 of last byte to o_cs_n high (trail); Value: D
Item: Minimum o_cs_n high time between bursts (gap); Value: D
Item: Byte period inside a continuous burst; Value: 16·D
Item: o_cs_n low time of an n-byte continuous burst; Value: 16·n·D + D
Item: Minimum time between first acceptances of consecutive n-byte bursts; Value: 16·n·D + 2·D
Item: Minimum period of single-byte bursts (i_cmd_last always 1); Value: 18·D
At f(i_clk) = 50 MHz:
D: 1; SCLK: 25 MHz; Byte period: 0.32 µs
D: 4; SCLK: 6.25 MHz; Byte period: 1.28 µs
D: 255; SCLK: about 98.04 kHz; Byte period: 81.6 µs
Conditions for a continuous burst (no SCLK pause):
The next command must be valid in the last cycle of the current transfer.
o_rsp_valid must be 0 in that cycle.
This means the response of the previous transfer was taken within 16·D − 1 cycles of becoming valid, for example with i_rsp_ready held at 1.
Back-pressure:
If o_rsp_valid = 1 in the last cycle of a transfer, the next transfer is not started at its SCLK edge 16.
The burst enters Pause (or Trail if it was the last byte).
If the shown byte has still not been taken at the end of a running transfer, that transfer's byte becomes the held byte.
No new transfer starts until both bytes have been taken.
Ordering: responses come out in command order (REQ-RSP-002).
Example 1: single-byte burst, D = 1, mode 0.
Command i_cmd_data = 8'hA5, i_cmd_last = 1.
The slave returns 8'h3C. i_rsp_ready = 1 throughout.
Cycle n is the cycle starting at edge n.
Edge 0 is the acceptance edge A. i_miso is driven by a mode-0 slave: bit 7 when o_cs_n falls, the next bit after each falling SCLK edge.
Cycle: −1; i_cmd_valid: 1; o_cmd_ready: 1; o_cs_n: 1; o_sclk: 0; o_mosi: 0; i_miso: 0; o_rsp_valid: 0; o_rsp_data: 00; Note: Command presented, handshake at edge 0
Cycle: 0; i_cmd_valid: 0; o_cmd_ready: 0; o_cs_n: 0; o_sclk: 0; o_mosi: 1 (d7); i_miso: 0 (r7); o_rsp_valid: 0; o_rsp_data: 00; Note: o_cs_n falls, d7 launched
Cycle: 1; i_cmd_valid: 0; o_cmd_ready: 0; o_cs_n: 0; o_sclk: 1; o_mosi: 1; i_miso: 0; o_rsp_valid: 0; o_rsp_data: 00; Note: SCLK edge 1 (rising): r7 = 0 captured at edge 1
Cycle: 2; i_cmd_valid: 0; o_cmd_ready: 0; o_cs_n: 0; o_sclk: 0; o_mosi: 0 (d6); i_miso: 0 (r6); o_rsp_valid: 0; o_rsp_data: 00; Note: SCLK edge 2 (falling, shift)
Cycle: 3; i_cmd_valid: 0; o_cmd_ready: 0; o_cs_n: 0; o_sclk: 1; o_mosi: 0; i_miso: 0; o_rsp_valid: 0; o_rsp_data: 00; Note: Edge 3: r6 = 0 captured
Cycle: 4; i_cmd_valid: 0; o_cmd_ready: 0; o_cs_n: 0; o_sclk: 0; o_mosi: 1 (d5); i_miso: 1 (r5); o_rsp_valid: 0; o_rsp_data: 00

Example 3: back-pressure, any D.
Byte N is shown at edge A_N + 16·D.
Transfer N+1 starts at that edge.
i_rsp_ready stays 0.
At edge A_N + 32·D, byte N+1 becomes the held byte and the burst enters Pause (or Trail), because o_rsp_valid = 1 forced o_cmd_ready = 0 in the last cycle.
When i_rsp_ready goes to 1, byte N is taken at edge H.
Byte N+1 is loaded at H and o_rsp_valid stays 1.
Byte N+1 is taken at edge H + 1.
After that, o_cmd_ready returns to 1 in Pause.
The block has no software-visible registers.
The block has no error output.
Every case below has a defined behaviour.

[REQ-ERR-001] When i_cpol or i_cpha changes while o_cs_n = 0 (an environment violation), the master shall not detect or report it and shall keep using CPOL_b and CPHA_b until the end of the burst (REQ-MODE-003).
[REQ-ERR-002] When i_cpol differs from CPOL_b at the edge where o_cs_n rises, o_sclk shall change to i_cpol at that edge (REQ-SCLK-006).
[REQ-ERR-003] When i_cmd_valid = 1 while o_cmd_ready = 0, the command shall wait without effect until a command handshake occurs.
[REQ-ERR-004] When i_cmd_valid = 1 while i_rst_n = 0, the master shall not accept the command (REQ-RST-007).
[REQ-ERR-005] When the response consumer never takes a response, the master shall keep o_rsp_valid = 1 with the same byte and shall not start any further transfer.
[REQ-ERR-006] When a burst is in Pause and no command ever arrives, o_cs_n shall stay 0 indefinitely.

[REQ-ERR-007] When i_rst_n is asserted during a transfer, o_cs_n shall go to 1 and o_sclk to i_cpol at once, even in the middle of an SCLK half period, and the partial byte shall be discarded (REQ-RST-008).
[REQ-ERR-008] When i_rst_n is asserted in Pause, Trail or the Idle gap, the master shall go to the reset state of REQ-RST-002 to REQ-RST-006, and pending bytes shall be discarded.
[REQ-ERR-009] A response handshake at exactly edge A + 16·D of a transfer shall make the received byte of that transfer load into o_rsp_data at that edge, with o_rsp_valid staying 1 (REQ-RSP-003).
[REQ-ERR-010] A timing violation on i_miso (data changing too close to a sampling edge) shall not be detected.
The captured bit is then undefined.
Other corner cases:
Case: i_cmd_last = 1 on every command; Behaviour: Every byte is its own burst. Minimum period 18·D cycles.
Case: i_cmd_last = 0 forever; Behaviour: The burst never ends. o_cs_n stays 0 and transfers continue as commands arrive.

Case: D = 1; Behaviour: Each SCLK half period is 1 cycle (SCLK = f(i_clk)/2). Lead, trail and minimum gap are 1 cycle. o_cmd_ready in Idle is NOT o_rsp_valid from the cycle in which o_cs_n rises (REQ-CMD-007 gives no blocked cycle; REQ-CMD-006 still holds). A shift edge and the next sampling edge are 1 cycle apart.
Case: D = 255; Behaviour: Each half period is 255 cycles and a byte takes 4080 cycles. The half-period count must reach 255 without overflow.
Case: Mode change between bursts; Behaviour: Allowed in any Idle cycle, including the cycle just before the acceptance edge. The new values are captured at the acceptance edge.

ID: CFG-MIN; Parameter values: PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV=1; Purpose: Smallest legal divider (SCLK = f(i_clk)/2), all four SPI modes

The verification runs every configuration listed here (run_set.json).
The SPI mode is a run-time input, so each configuration runs all four modes.
Environment obligations (protocol duties of the blocks that drive the inputs):
[ENV-001] The environment shall release i_rst_n synchronously to i_clk.
Assertion may be asynchronous.
[ENV-002] The environment shall keep i_cmd_valid = 0 while i_rst_n = 0.
[ENV-003] The environment shall change i_cpol and i_cpha only while o_cs_n = 1.
Error tests may violate this rule on purpose to check REQ-ERR-001.
[ENV-004] The SPI slave (testbench model) shall drive i_miso from o_sclk and o_cs_n only.
With CPHA = 0 it puts bit 7 when o_cs_n falls and the next bit after each trailing SCLK edge.
With CPHA = 1 it puts bit 7 − j after leading SCLK edge 2·j + 1.
[ENV-005] The slave model shall change i_miso only after the i_clk edge at which o_sclk or o_cs_n changed, never in a way that changes the value seen at a sampling edge.
[ENV-007] The environment shall not assert i_rst_n at an edge of i_clk: assertion happens between edges (in silicon, outside the recovery/removal window of the reset flops).
An edge that coincides with the assertion is not a legal case and no check covers it (GAP-001).
[ENV-008] The environment shall drive i_rst_n = 0 from the start of operation (time zero in simulation), before the first rising edge of i_clk, for at least 2 cycles.
Before the first assertion of i_rst_n the outputs are undefined and no check applies. i_cpol, i_cpha and every other input shall always be 0 or 1, never X or Z (GAP-002).
[ENV-006] In silicon, i_miso shall meet setup and hold time to i_clk at each sampling edge.
With D = 1, the slave clock-to-output plus the board round trip must fit in one i_clk period minus setup time.
The command stream is not required to keep i_cmd_valid, i_cmd_data or i_cmd_last stable before acceptance (REQ-CMD-004).
The response consumer may drive i_rsp_ready with any pattern.
Checks and special setups:
[VER-001] The verification shall run all four modes in every configuration of section 11, with random bytes on i_cmd_data and from the slave model.
[VER-002] The verification shall use burst lengths 1, 2 and at least 16, and shall mix bursts with and without pauses (i_cmd_valid gaps of 0, 1 and many cycles).
[VER-003] A scoreboard shall check that each response equals the byte sent by the slave during the matching command, in order, with no loss or duplicate (REQ-RSP-001, REQ-RSP-002, REQ-RSP-011).
[VER-004] A slave-side monitor shall check MOSI data at every sampling edge and the SCLK edge times (A + k·D).
It shall also check the lead, trail and gap times, the SCLK idle level and that o_mosi never changes at a sampling edge.
[VER-005] The verification shall check o_cmd_ready cycle by cycle against REQ-CMD-006 to REQ-CMD-012, including the blocked first D − 1 Idle cycles.
[VER-006] Back-pressure tests shall hold i_rsp_ready = 0 for long periods so that a held byte is created.
They shall cover a response handshake exactly at edge A + 16·D (REQ-ERR-009) and random i_rsp_ready patterns.

[VER-007] Reset tests shall hold i_rsp_ready = 0 before the reset where a shown or held byte is wanted, and shall assert i_rst_n between i_clk edges in each phase (Transfer, Pause, Trail, Idle gap, with a held byte).
They shall check that outputs take reset values at once and that no response of the aborted transfer appears.
[VER-008] A test shall toggle i_cpol while i_rst_n = 0 and in Idle, and check that o_sclk follows it in the same cycle (REQ-SCLK-005, REQ-RST-003).
[VER-009] A test shall change i_cpol and i_cpha in the cycle just before a burst-start acceptance edge and check that the new values are used.
[VER-010] An error test shall change i_cpol and i_cpha during a burst and check that the burst finishes in the captured mode (REQ-ERR-001, REQ-ERR-002).
[VER-011] Coverage shall include:
Mode × configuration.
Continuous join (Example 2).
Pause entry and exit.
Held byte created and released.
Reset in each phase.
i_cmd_last = 1 on the first byte.
Behaviour visible only through the ports:
The held byte is seen only through response order and o_cmd_ready.
CPOL_b and CPHA_b are seen only through o_sclk, o_mosi and the received data when the inputs change during a burst.
REQ-PAR-001 is checked by elaborating once with an illegal value, not by simulation.
[REQ-IMP-001] The block shall meet timing at 50 MHz i_clk (20 ns period) in the GF180MCU technology, at worst-case corner.
[REQ-IMP-002] The RTL shall follow docs/RTL_RULES.md (REF-003).
[REQ-IMP-003] All flip-flops shall be clocked on the rising edge of i_clk and reset asynchronously by i_rst_n.
The RTL shall contain no latches, no clock gating and no derived clocks.
[REQ-IMP-004] o_cs_n and o_mosi shall be driven directly by flip-flops.
[REQ-IMP-005] While o_cs_n = 0, o_sclk shall come from a flip-flop value.
The only combinational path from an input to o_sclk shall be the i_cpol path used while o_cs_n = 1 or during reset.
[REQ-IMP-006] o_sclk should be free of glitches when o_cs_n changes.
The selection between i_cpol and the internal SCLK value should be built so that equal inputs give no static hazard.
[REQ-IMP-007] o_cmd_ready, o_rsp_valid and o_rsp_data shall be driven by flip-flops or by logic of flip-flops only.
They shall have no combinational path from any input.
[REQ-IMP-008] i_miso shall be captured directly into a data flip-flop with no synchroniser.
The integrator shall constrain the input delay of i_miso.
[REQ-IMP-009] The half-period counter shall be wide enough for D = 255 (at least 8 bits).
The area budget has not been given (open question OQ-004).
The block is expected to be small: one byte each of shift-out, shift-in, response and held storage, plus counters.

Should a transfer also be allowed to start when the shown byte is taken in the last cycle (combinational i_rsp_ready to o_cmd_ready) to avoid a pause?
Decided: no. A transfer starts only when o_rsp_valid = 0 at the acceptance edge (DEC-002); no combinational path from i_rsp_ready
Is D = 1 (25 MHz SCLK at 50 MHz) meant for real slaves, given the 20 ns MISO round-trip budget?
Decided: D = 1 stays legal and verified in simulation. Silicon timing is an integrator duty (ENV-006)
Should o_mosi be driven to 0 (or 1) in Idle instead of holding its last value?
Decided: o_mosi holds its last value outside transfers (DEC-005)
What is the area budget on GF180MCU?
Decided: no area budget. Synthesis area is reported for information only
Should Pause have a timeout that releases o_cs_n?
Decided: no timeout; o_cs_n stays low in Pause until the next command
Should the master enforce o_cs_n high for at least D cycles after reset release?
Decided: no. The minimum gap is not guaranteed across a reset (REQ-RST-011)
Should CFG-MAX stay in the run set (longer simulation)?
Decided: CFG-MAX (D = 255) stays in the run set
